body: Update test project for now is in this branch: https://github.com/BastiaanOlij/test-custom-shader-templates/tree/ldotn_template

@clayjohn @DarioSamo I think this is pretty much in working condition and as far as I want to take the foundation. I am tempted to add template support to the compatibility renderer as well but might do that in a follow up.

A few things I'd like to discuss with you before taking this out of draft.

- Dario, for you specifically, I ended up not touching the mutex around shader compilation, so that works as before. I'm still tempted on moving it into the ShaderTemplate class but we'd need to move part of the pipeline creation in there then as well.
- I'm also not 100% sure if we've got caching right, and if there is any further impact on the shader baking logic. I think it works correctly, but could use an extra set of eyes on this.
- There is a bit of confusion with naming atm. User shaders now refer to the template they are using, but inside our template the object that contains the template code is also called shader for historic reasons (since we only ever had one). I wonder if we should choose some better names here (e.g. `MaterialStorage::ShaderTemplate::shader`), same with all the `shader_template_*` functions that now refer to the shader, we may want to come up with better naming.
- Even though the mobile renderer now uses shader groups, we still have some left over functions around versions.
- And on the subject of shader groups, I wonder if we should store these differently. Because we only ever had one template, we store the groups on that level, but now that we have multiple templates, they are enabled in unison. I think we can come up with something better for this.
- Currently you can't edit `.gdtemplate` files from the editor and we don't have functionality to save the built-in template(s) to a `.gdtemplate` file to function as a starting point. I think we should do this as a separate PR (same as with eventually deciding to have additional built-in includes). For now this [sample project](https://github.com/BastiaanOlij/test-custom-shader-templates/tree/ldotn_template) can be used but it includes only a bare bones implementation.
Can we have more uniforms than the standard include files specify? It would be common to bind some extra uniform buffers for custom shading models.

> Can we have more uniforms than the standard include files specify? It would be common to bind some extra uniform buffers for custom shading models.

At this point the only way to get extra uniforms in, is to add those in through the user shader that is embedded.

There was someone who did a PR on my old implementation to add in the ability to define additional uniforms in the template that would be exposed on the material. I think its worth revisiting that but as a follow up to the initial implementation.

One of the difficulties of getting this merged initially was that we were trying to do too much and reviewers don't see the wood for the trees anymore.

> Maybe I missed something, but it doesn't seem like new templates inherit previously enabled shader groups? Or does that not matter?

This is one that could probably do with a rethink and moving the group logic into the templates at a later date. However for now this logic remains implemented on the ShaderRD level. You can see that in both the forward+ and mobile renderers, when groups are enabled this is applied to all templates.

@Calinou got all of your comments sorted.

Docs should now be updated, and it should now check for double inclusion of "shader_template" in the user shader.

Live updating seems like a whole different thing to tackle, especially as this would be the same workload as making this work for gdshader, I think we should keep that out of scope for this PR.

Finally, agree that gdtemplate is a very ambiguous name. But I haven't heard an alternative yet that works better without it becoming very verbose.  Totally up for suggestions though...
Marked this as ready for review, I'm sure there will be more requests for changes.

> Finally, agree that gdtemplate is a very ambiguous name. But I haven't heard an alternative yet that works better without it becoming very verbose. Totally up for suggestions though...

Some ideas that would come to mind for me would be:
- `gdshader_template` or `template_gdshader`
- `gdshader_templ` or `templ_gdshader`
- `gdshader_type`
- `gdshader_model`

I would be in favor of having the connection with the `gdshader` file extension be clear from the template file extension. That might be verbose but I am not sure if being more verbose would be such a big concern. I mean for those that need to edit their paths for the `.gdextension` file to load the correct binary files they aren't complaining that much either about this specifically (and those string paths are LONG). You aren't doing it that regularly anyways as I imagine.

Ok, test project has been updated but for some reason the omni light only works in runtime, not in the editor, both in mobile and forward+. Haven't figured out why yet....

I've played around a little with this branch. As a test, without too much trouble I managed to modify how decals are blended to use them for drop shadows:
Screenshot
This was a minor problem I've eyed in a (toy) project of mine, so it's nice to see this feature offer a solution. I was thinking for a moment that a custom template might also allow you to add extra output buffers. But it seems like even though you can declare new outputs in the shader, there's no way to bind them correctly. So I assume that's simply not something this feature on its own will allow. I've taken note of some hitches I ran into. I imagine some of these may be expected or out-of-scope of this PR, but I'll mention everything just in case: 1. If several instances share a material that uses a custom template, only one of them renders. Try duplicating a node that uses a custom template, it won't render until you "Make Unique" the material. 2. When there's an error in a shader template, I get a giant overflowing error message popup. The editor also sometimes freezes for a quite a while when there's an error, which I suspect sure is also due to the error popup.
Screenshot
As a sidenote, these errors are very hard to parse even in the console output, because the actual error message is printed before the huge dump of shader code so it's easily lost. 3. The example uses `.gdshaderinc` for shader template includes, but this is inappropriate because they're not valid GDShader code and won't parse successfully when opened by the built-in shader editor. I don't think there's really any other suitable option for file extension out of the box either. The best choice currently seems to be using a custom extension like `gslslinc` and adding it as a TextFile extension in the editor settings. This is an existing problem for GLSL shaders, though. 4. Editing an included file doesn't trigger a recompile of the shader template. Again, existing problem for GLSL shaders, but it was a repeating annoyance when testing this. 5. Includes don't allow relative paths, which is inconsistent with .glsl shaders. 6. `ShaderTemplate` is an imported resource, so shouldn't .gdtemplate files have the "Import As" dropdown in the import panel? 7. With `#include "godot/*"` it seems like I can include only some arbitrary subset of the includes the default scene shader uses, but not all of them, which made copying the default shader to modify it more cumbersome. 8. It would be nice if clicking .gdtemplate files opened your external script editor if one is configured, since currently clicking them does basically nothing.

Thanks for checking out the work, awesome to get some feedback, not sure when I'll have time to actually work on this again but will be sure to take onboard what I can.

> 1. If several instances share a material that uses a custom template, only one of them renders. Try duplicating a node that uses a custom template, it won't render until you "Make Unique" the material.

This feels like a bug that was introduced along the way, it should definitely have no problem with the same material being used multiple times. 

> 2. When there's an error in a shader template, I get a giant overflowing error message popup. The editor also sometimes freezes for a quite a while when there's an error, which I suspect sure is also due to the error popup.
>     As a sidenote, these errors are very hard to parse even in the console output, because the actual error message is printed before the huge dump of shader code so it's easily lost.

Welcome to our world :) We have always had the same issue when working on the built-in shaders. When there is an error in the shader code, Godot will output the shader code. That it will attempt to compile 5 - 10 variants, each thousands of lines of code long, for every shader that uses the template code, quickly overpowers the log.

We usually have a breakpoint on the error routine and you quickly grab the right bit of output, but I agree that this could  use a rethink and much nicer solution. Outside of the scope of this PR though.
     
> 3. The example uses `.gdshaderinc` for shader template includes, but this is inappropriate because they're not valid GDShader code and won't parse successfully when opened by the built-in shader editor. I don't think there's really any other suitable option for file extension out of the box either. The best choice currently seems to be using a custom extension like `gslslinc` and adding it as a TextFile extension in the editor settings. This is an existing problem for GLSL shaders, though.

We mostly piggy back on the include system already present in Godot. We're dealing with existing choices here. Probably worth a follow up to improve on this.

> 4. Editing an included file doesn't trigger a recompile of the shader template. Again, existing problem for GLSL shaders, but it was a repeating annoyance when testing this.

Hmmm, strange, it's supposed to recompile them. Could be a focus thing because it's the re-import logic that should trigger the recompile when the template code is updated in memory.

> 5. Includes don't allow relative paths, which is inconsistent with .glsl shaders.

I struggled with this because there is a lot of existing structure in place that never assumed the template code came from a file. By the time the shader code gets processed it has long forgotten where the original template file is located. 

So something that would be nice to improve, but not sure it's worth the impact for a first version of this.

> 6. `ShaderTemplate` is an imported resource, so shouldn't .gdtemplate files have the "Import As" dropdown in the import panel?

Probably, not sure how that is triggered, will have to look into that.

> 7. With `#include "godot/*"` it seems like I can include only some arbitrary subset of the includes the default scene shader uses, but not all of them, which made copying the default shader to modify it more cumbersome.

Indeed, they are specifically added by calling `ShaderIncludeDB::register_built_in_include_file`.
Originally I restructure some of the key includes and made them available as well. This was one of the things we decided to remove when breaking up the work.

The main concern here is that any include file we expose, backs us into a corner once we decide to restructure things. The include files were never organised with the idea that we'd expose them to users at some point.

So this will require some more thought and work before we're ready to expose more.

> 8. It would be nice if clicking .gdtemplate files opened your external script editor if one is configured, since currently clicking them does basically nothing.

Indeed, I'm not familiar enough with this part of the editor though so not sure how easy it is to add that in.

Rebased this to the latest master. Also updated the sample project (and merged stuff into its master branch), there were several changes to the rendering code in Godot master that broke the templates in the sample project. Bit of a PITA :)

@Nallebeorn I was not able to reproduce the issue where it wouldn't reload template changes. That worked fine for me, they were being reloaded properly whenever Godot got focus (I am using an external editor to edit the files).

> I was not able to reproduce the issue where it wouldn't reload template changes. That worked fine for me, they were being reloaded properly whenever Godot got focus (I am using an external editor to edit the files).

Yeah, reloading when editing the gdtemplate file works fine for me too. It's editing files that are _included_ by the template, like the gdshaderinc files in the sample project, that doesn't trigger a reimport. But it looks like this is a known issue for glsl shaders already: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/72281, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/76024

> Yeah, reloading when editing the gdtemplate file works fine for me too. It's editing files that are _included_ by the template, like the gdshaderinc files in the sample project, that doesn't trigger a reimport. But it looks like this is a known issue for glsl shaders already: #72281, #76024

Ah gotcha!

No idea how to manage dependencies with that, someone with more knowledge of the editor itself might be able to shed light on that...

Tested locally, I get an error on the [testing project](https://github.com/BastiaanOlij/test-custom-shader-templates)'s `master` branch in Forward+'s `res://forward/standard.gdshaderinc`: `res://forward/fragment.gdshaderinc` also has an error: I assume this happens because these files have GDShader include extensions, but they're actually GLSL. I would suggest using `.glsl.inc` as a file extension in this case, so that they can't be edited through the shader editor as it's not currently intended to be used for GLSL editing. It's not really an issue with this PR, more of a question of style guide and standards for the documentation.

Considering I am really waiting for https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13480 to be implemented I wanted a general place to voice my support/need for this, which I have chosen to be in here because it seems to be the path that actually moves forward/is currently close to merging
